newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Foreigners still far below Taiwan stock ceiling.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners still far below Taiwan stock ceiling.

text.p: Foreign investors have remitted US$11.154 billion into Taiwan's sizzling stock market, leaving room for $82.458 billion more before hitting the official ceiling, the central bank said on Friday.
Foreign investors currently may put up to $93.612 billion in the market under rules capping foreign holdings at 25 percent of the bourse's market value, the bank said in a statement.
In September 1996, the bank raised the ceiling to 25 percent from 20 percent and allowed foreign individuals to trade Taiwan stocks.
In June, foreign funds remitted into the market totalled $871 million, up from US$731 million in May, but down from a 1997 monthly high $1.39 billion in March, the bank said.
A total of $926 million of such funds flowed out of Taiwan in June, down from May's $1.12 billion.
Aside from direct stock market holdings, the bank has allowed inflows of $2.037 billion in funds raised overseas by local firms through convertible bonds and global depositary receipts.
In this category, foreigners as of July 8 had remitted $753 million into Taiwan and could send $1.284 billion more before reaching a legal ceiling, the bank said.
